name: Bronson Forest Recreation Site - Peck Lake Campground
note: The recreation site's second campground, on a narrow strip of land between Peck Lake and an arm of Little Fishing Lake about 3 km north of the Little Fishing Lake campground (own entry), reached by Peck Lake Road off Highway 21. A lakeside row of 20 sites faces the campground beach, playground and boat launch; a second loop of 21 sites sits in the pines about 400 m southeast. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: Sask Parks booking site parks.saskatchewan.ca SKPP parkId 290510 (Bronson Forest Recreation Site), loop filter 'Peck Lake' (loop id 290745), read 2026-11-19: 41 site-specific electric sites P1-P42 (no P25), 33 'Nightly Electric' + 8 'Seasonal Electric' (P21, P22, P27, P28, P29, P31, P35, P42); every site's detail page read: 'Maximum Equipment Length (ft)' 40 on 11 nightly sites, 32 on 14, 25 on 7 ('Camping Unit 19 to 25ft' allowed), 18 on P30 only, so 32 nightly sites take a 23-ft rig; gravel pads, back-in/roadside. Sask Parks Peck Lake Campground map (bronson-forest-all.pdf p.4, dated 2026-04-10) draws the lakeside row P1-P20 and the loop P21-P42 with a self-registration station. Not a duplicate: 9163 Little Fishing Lake is 2.9 km away (GIS centroids), 3.5 km by road via Peck Lake Road and Highway 21 (OSRM); nothing else in the DB within 10 km. A real public drive-in RV campground a 23-ft rig fits. Provincial: no price gate. (phase-7 SK lead 9, found p3-530) --Claude
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-19. Every Peck Lake paging row reads 'Near Water - no'. Esri World_Imagery z17 (0.70 m/px, rendered; z18 'Map data not yet available') with all 41 SKPP GIS points: the north side of the lakeside row (P12-P20) faces Peck Lake across open sand and grass with scattered pines; pixel transects put the water's edge about 20-25 m from P13, ~25 m from P14, ~32 m from P16, ~35 m from P18 and ~38 m from P20. That strip is the park's 'Peck Lake Campground Beach' (Tourism SK listing 372: 'fine, soft sand, and a grassy park and playground area'), with the beach and playground symbols on the 2026-04-10 campground map and a concrete picnic pad, benches and the boat-launch/kitchen day-use area at the east end. SKPP site photos (read 2026-11-19) show Peck Lake across that open ground from P13, P14, P15, P16, P17, P18 and P19. The south side (P1-P10) faces an arm of Little Fishing Lake ~30-50 m away behind a continuous tree band; the loop P21-P42 is ~150 m+ from water in forest. Lakefront not earned: the open ground between the sites and the water is a used beach/playground/picnic area, not an unused apron, and the agency flags no site near water. Lakeview rests on P13-P19 (nightly, 32-40 ft). --Claude

flags: SEPARATE FROM 9163: Peck Lake lakeside-row centroid 53.87646,-109.58735 vs Little Fishing Lake centroid ~53.8547,-109.5631 = 2.9 km; own access, Peck Lake Road to Highway 21 (OSRM 3.5 km between them). Same SKPP park page and booking (parkId 290510, loop filter).

PIN: placed on the lakeside row (centroid of P1-P20, 53.8765,-109.5874). The SKPP park page's 'Geography' point 53.87649,-109.58610 sits at P1/P2; its 'Getting There' GPS 53.85375,-109.56194 is the Little Fishing Lake campground. The second loop P21-P42 centres ~53.8746,-109.5825 (~380 m SE); OSM names that loop 'Peck Lake Overflow Campground', but SKPP sells it as part of Peck Lake (13 nightly + 8 seasonal).

WATERFRONT: lakeview, not lakefront. P13-P20 are ~20-38 m from Peck Lake across open sand/grass with scattered pines, but that ground is the park's campground beach + playground + picnic area and every SKPP row says 'Near Water - no'. AWH may judge P13-P15 (nearest, ~20-30 m) as clear lakefront sites; the evidence is in waterfront_evidence.
